Here's the problem with this idea of illegal vs legal. People are treating this idea as if there is some black and white interpretation of the law. That's simply not the case. If you recall the Anderson Cooper story during the /r/jailbait kerfuffle, one the lawyers he was speaking argued that she believed that even if the pics were non-nude, it could still be argued that the pics were illegal under certain circumstances. You may argue that she's wrong and I'd actually lean towards you being correct, but if someone really got a bug in their ass to push the issue, that's a possible legal battle and a lot of unwanted attention for Voat. They don't have the resources the combat such claims and SJW's seem to be intent on deconstructing anything on the internet that is not a safe space for them.

Yes, the issue isn't as simple as just reading the law, it's all about how it's interpreted and enforced by courts. To reasonably judge whether something is illegal or not you need someone with experience in that specific area of the law (i.e. a lawyer) who also knows how courts have handled that specific issue. And even if a precedent has been set for something courts can still rule against that, especially if it's not a simple case.

Ultimately the legality of something can only be determined at 100% surity in a court case, which take time, effort, and other resources. Even though Voat probably isn't obliged to remove anything from the site without a court order, the only realistic option (at least at this point) is to remove and disallow content that would most likely be determined illegal in court.

  • Add/remove a Set from:
    • voat.co/sets
    • voat.co/mysets

Keyboard Shortcuts:

Click on a post or a comment to select it. examples: post, comment.

On a selected posts you can press:

  • Z to downvote

Fixed element position:
